lead: Nine days to the 4 November local elections. Durban is still tense after a week of attacks on foreign nationals, the mini-budget's fuel levy cut lands on election day, and abroad, Serbia's president has conceded defeat to a student-led movement.

items.title: Five held after deadly attacks on foreign nationals in Durban
items.summary: KZN police took in five men for questioning on Friday after a foreign national was beaten to death in the CBD on Thursday and others were assaulted in Berea. The unrest traces back to a Home Affairs asylum directive, issued after a Constitutional Court ruling and withdrawn on 9 October.

items.title: Mini-budget: growth cut to 1.2%, fuel levy relief from 4 November
items.summary: Treasury lowered its 2026 growth forecast from 1.6% to 1.2%. A further R10bn funds a temporary levy cut of R3/litre on diesel and R1.50/litre on petrol from 4 November to 1 December, with a smaller cut running to 5 January. R5.1bn was reprioritised for gender-based violence services.

items.title: IEC turns down MK party's request to change its candidate list
items.summary: The Electoral Commission rejected MK's bid to alter its list for the 4 November local elections; the party said some councillors were left off and others had died, and says it distrusts the IEC.

items.title: Pretoria CBD tap water declared safe again
items.summary: Tshwane lifted its precautionary boil-water advisory for the CBD on Saturday. A probe into contamination at the Bronkhorstspruit supply continues.

items.title: Serbia's Vucic concedes defeat to student protest movement
items.summary: After Sunday's parliamentary election, Vucic said his party had lost; his own sample put the Students' List at 135 to 140 seats against about 105 for his party. Turnout was reported at 70%, the highest since 1992.

items.title: Israel votes on Tuesday with neither bloc near a majority
items.summary: Polls put an opposition bloc around Gadi Eisenkot at about 52 seats and Netanyahu's camp at about 50, both short of 61. Arab-led parties could decide who governs.

items.title: Russian strikes kill 8 across Ukraine as talks are pencilled in for after 4 November
items.summary: A drone hit a residential building in Vinnytsia during an overnight wave of more than 150 drones. The Kremlin says trilateral talks with Ukraine and the US could resume after its 4 November holiday.

items.title: Cost-of-living protests turn violent across Europe
items.summary: France reported close to 1,000 arrests over the weekend, Italy deployed soldiers in Milan and other cities, and police used tear gas in Tirana.

items.title: China's Communist Party opens a four-day plenum today
items.summary: The Fifth Plenum runs 26 to 29 October in Beijing. Markets are watching for signals on consumer demand, fiscal support and local-government debt.

items.title: Rand steady near R16.50 after an oil-driven slide
items.summary: The rand traded around 16.51 to the dollar on Friday morning after falling sharply on Thursday as high oil prices weighed. Local data this week: leading indicator (Tue), private credit and producer inflation (Thu), trade balance (Fri).

items.title: Big central bank week: Fed on Wednesday, ECB Thursday
items.summary: The Fed is widely expected to hold at 3.75 to 4.00% on Wednesday. Microsoft and Alphabet report Wednesday and Amazon Thursday, with AI spending in focus.

items.title: Bok injury worries ahead of the November tour
items.summary: Eben Etzebeth is awaiting assessment on a lower-limb injury and Cheslin Kolbe is doubtful after breaking his jaw; RG Snyman and Kwagga Smith are not expected back. The four-Test tour opens against Italy in Turin on 7 November.

items.title: Premier League: Villa beat City, United thrashed at home
items.summary: Aston Villa beat Manchester City 2-1, Spurs won 2-0 at Chelsea, and Bournemouth won 3-0 at Old Trafford. Arsenal and Liverpool both won 2-0 ahead of next Sunday's meeting at Anfield.
